rubric: The workshop title is clearly the dominant element and is much larger than every other piece of text.
The date, time and place are easy to find, grouped together, and use no more than about three levels of emphasis overall.
Lines are set comfortably: sensible line length and line-height, no awkward one-word last lines, and no clipped or cramped text.
The card uses a small, consistent set of type styles (one or two families, few sizes and weights) with consistent alignment.
All text, including the smallest line, has strong contrast and is readable at phone size.

result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both cards leave out the sign-up URL. B fits everything comfortably in the frame and groups when, where, cost and what to bring into one clean, aligned block. A has a bigger, more dominant title, but its card runs off the bottom edge, there's a lot of uneven empty space, and the tan 'FREE' text and the tiny WHEN/WHERE labels are low-contrast. B's white-on-tan chips are also weak on contrast, but its layout is more consistent and easier to read overall. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Neither card shows the sign-up URL eastmoor.example/bread, and both repeat FREE and use some low-contrast white-on-tan text. B's title is more dominant and its When/Where blocks are clearer, but it switches from left-aligned to centered text and the card runs off the bottom edge. A is the tidier and more consistent of the two: one centered composition with all the details in a single box.
